answer: Identity-Weighted Coordination Windows: each identity must anchor a distinct kernel of routing history through a shared river of transaction relays before its votes carry weight. The protocol caps unproven identities at one relay per epoch, so forging N credible agents costs N epochs of sustained bandwidth and latency, paid per identity. Coordinated clusters also lose quorum priority at the knoll of each window, taxing attackers who must fund real infrastructure longer than honest agents.
